messages:
maya: FYI bringing up umbra14b int4 on canary last night — seeing fragmentation + OOMs when bursty traffic hits. max_new_tokens default 512 seems to blow slots.

devon: Can you paste the runtime config + batch settings?

maya: Here's the canary config: ```
model: umbra14b
quant: int4
prefetch: true
prefetch_slots: 8
batch: {max_batch_tokens: 2048, max_latency_ms: 80}
max_new_tokens: 512
kv_eviction: LRU
```

alex: Interesting — prefetch_slots 8 is high for int4; that can increase cached KV and fragmentation. Try `prefetch_slots: 2` and batch `max_batch_tokens -> 1024`.

riley: Also check cold-start vs warmed node diffs. Are OOMs during steady-state or ramp-up?

maya: Mostly ramp-up. Logs show OOMs at token 60-100 into generation under concurrent 6 requests. Attaching snippet: ```
OOM at alloc 1.2GB (kv cache growth). Node free: 400MB
stack: alloc_tensor
```

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-452 umbra14b canary oom. Pager disabled (low severity)

devon: If it's KV growth, enable `kv_trim_threshold: 0.6` and set `kv_prefetch_limit: 1` for int4 models. Also set `max_new_tokens` default to `256` for this model in the model-profiles.

alex: We should add an automatic fallback route to a quantized-compat variant with smaller prefetch on surge. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll test config changes now. Quick question — how do you propose we roll the default change? per-model param in catalog or rollout via canary with traffic split?

riley: Per-model config in catalog + canary rollout. Update model-profile, create canary with 10% traffic, monitor token-level errors and OOM rate.

maya: @devon can you add an eval that replays our ramp test w/ prompts? want perf + quality delta for int4 tweaks

devon: On it. I'll add an automated eval job: `replay_ramp(umbra14b, q=int4, pref=2, max_new=256)` — will attach perf/quality plots to the job.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: model-profile update umbra14b max_new_tokens=256 prefetch_slots=2 kv_trim_threshold=0.6 -> canary @10%

maya: thx — will report back after 2h. initial local sim: lower mem usage by ~35% and no OOMs in 100-run ramp. Quality diff looks negligible on top-1 for our prompts.

alex: Great. If canary looks good, we should also add a regression alert comparing perplexity and hit-rate vs baseline before full rollout.

riley: Also add a short-lived metric to track `kv_growth/sec` to detect regressions post-rollout.

maya: noted — I'll create the monitor and link the dashboard.
